title: Unmasking Implicit Bias: Evaluating Persona-Prompted LLM Responses in Power-Disparate Social Scenarios

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring semantic shifts via cosine distance and evaluating response quality via an LLM-judged Helpful-Honest-Harmless (HHH) preference win rate when assigning specific racial personas in power-disparate social scenarios.

Calculating the standard deviation of cosine distances and HHH win rates between demographically-prompted (e.g., male, female, non-binary, transgender) and non-demographically-prompted responses to evaluate response variability.
Comparing semantic shifts and LLM-judged response quality (HHH criteria) when incorporating age-related personas (e.g., young, middle-aged, old) into prompts for simulated social interactions.

Assessing demographic sensitivity and response quality bias by measuring the difference in generated outputs when religious identities (e.g., Christian, Muslim, Buddhist, Jewish, Atheist) are injected into social scenario prompts.

Evaluating semantic deviations and win-rate preferences in LLM outputs when assigning political stance personas (Conservative, Liberal, Centrist) to subjects and responders interacting in varied social contexts.

Measuring implicit biases by comparing the cosine distance and LLM-judged HHH quality of responses generated with disabled (physically or mentally) versus abled personas across scenarios with and without power disparities.
Evaluating shifts in response semantics and quality (Helpful, Honest, Harmless) when interactants are identified by nationality statuses such as native-born citizen, immigrant, or migrant worker.

Analyzing the variance in LLM-generated response embeddings and HHH preference win rates when personas are described using physical appearance traits (e.g., ugly-looking, average-looking, attractive-looking).
